# 29. Pre-Launch / Launch / Post-Launch

<!-- Generated by tools/build_checklists.py. Edit the generator to change checklist structure. -->

**Purpose:** Control the final release sequence so launch is verified, reversible, measurable, and followed by stabilization checks.

## Universal Constraints
- [ ] The solution must remain static front-end only: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, images, fonts, documents, and generated static files only.
- [ ] The stack must avoid proprietary lock-in, paid builders, paid plugins, closed hosting features that cannot be replaced, and opaque third-party scripts where an open or free-tier-friendly alternative exists.
- [ ] Every decision must be documented as a quality rule, acceptance criterion, or exception with rationale; implementation notes belong outside the checklist.
- [ ] Every checklist item must be testable by review, automated audit, source inspection, browser testing, or client sign-off.
- [ ] Manual exceptions must record the owner, reason, expiration date, affected pages, and residual risk.

## Must Exist
- [ ] A pre-launch gate covering content, design, accessibility, SEO, performance, analytics, forms, security, legal, hosting, and client approval.
- [ ] A launch runbook with owner, timing, DNS changes, deploy steps, smoke tests, rollback plan, and communication plan.
- [ ] A production checklist for domain, HTTPS, redirects, headers, sitemap, robots, forms, analytics, and critical pages.
- [ ] A post-launch monitoring checklist for 24 hours, 72 hours, 7 days, and 30 days.
- [ ] A backup of the previous site or rollback artifact where applicable.
- [ ] A Search Console or webmaster verification plan where the client uses search platforms.
- [ ] A post-launch issue log with severity, owner, and resolution status.
- [ ] A client sign-off record for launch readiness and known exceptions.

## Must Be True
- [ ] No launch may proceed with unresolved blockers unless a qualified owner accepts the risk in writing.
- [ ] Production metadata must use production URLs only.
- [ ] Staging and preview pages must be blocked from indexing or removed.
- [ ] Forms and analytics must be tested on the production domain.
- [ ] DNS changes must be scheduled with awareness of TTL and rollback implications.
- [ ] The launch must include a smoke test from a clean browser and mobile device.
- [ ] Post-launch checks must verify real user paths, not only homepage availability.
- [ ] Known issues must be transparent to stakeholders.

## Must Be Checked
- [ ] Check homepage, priority service pages, contact, forms, legal pages, sitemap, robots, 404, and redirects immediately after deploy.
- [ ] Check HTTPS, canonical host, mixed content, security headers, and cache behavior.
- [ ] Check Search Console submission or equivalent where applicable.
- [ ] Check analytics events after consent choices.
- [ ] Check form delivery, autoresponders, spam handling, and thank-you pages.
- [ ] Check page speed and Core Web Vitals lab indicators after production deploy.
- [ ] Check that old important URLs redirect or have planned replacements.
- [ ] Check post-launch logs for 404s, blocked assets, unusual traffic drops, and user-reported issues.

## Must Be Avoided
- [ ] Avoid launching late in the day without monitoring coverage.
- [ ] Avoid changing DNS, content, tracking, and hosting all at once without rollback clarity.
- [ ] Avoid leaving placeholder noindex, robots blocks, staging titles, or test analytics IDs in production.
- [ ] Avoid skipping form tests because they worked locally.
- [ ] Avoid deleting the old site before the new production path is verified.
- [ ] Avoid post-launch silence after handoff.

## Premium Acceptance Standard
- [ ] Launch must be a controlled release with evidence.
- [ ] The first post-launch week must focus on stability, indexing, forms, analytics, and user-reported defects.
- [ ] Every launch exception must have an owner and deadline.
- [ ] The site must enter maintenance with clear next actions.

## Automation Hooks
- [ ] Run the audit script before launch and immediately after production deployment.
- [ ] Use JSON reports to compare pre-launch and post-launch status.

## Detailed Best-Practice Review Areas
- [ ] Pre-launch confirms final content, design, page list, navigation, footer, CTAs, SEO metadata, legal pages, forms, analytics, domain, hosting, repository, deployment, HTTPS, sitemap, robots, 404, and rollback.
- [ ] Launch QA verifies live homepage, inner pages, navigation, forms, assets, CSS, JS, images, video/fallbacks, favicon, 404, sitemap, robots, metadata, social previews, analytics, redirects, and domain/HTTPS behavior.
- [ ] Post-launch checks Search Console/search tools, indexing, sitemap submission, crawl errors, analytics, form delivery, traffic/conversions, performance, accessibility, 404s, broken links, monitoring alerts, and first improvement list.
- [ ] Launch blocks include broken forms, broken HTTPS, exposed secrets, private files, staging references, localhost URLs, missing legal pages, missing 404/sitemap/robots, critical accessibility failures, and production robots blocking.

## Report Output Required
- [ ] Report every failed automated check with severity, checklist category, issue code, affected file or page, evidence, whether it is script-fixable, and how to fix it.
- [ ] Report every manual-only failure with reviewer, affected page or component, expected standard, actual behavior, recommended fix, owner, and target date.
- [ ] Separate launch blockers from quality improvements so critical static-site failures cannot be hidden by low-priority polish notes.
- [ ] Attach the JSON audit report, Markdown audit report, screenshots where visual proof is needed, and manual QA evidence for browser, device, keyboard, screen reader, form, analytics, and live deployment checks.

## Evidence Required
- [ ] Record reviewed pages, tools used, dates, reviewers, unresolved exceptions, and links to generated reports.
- [ ] Attach screenshots or source references for failures that cannot be proven by automated reports.
- [ ] Mark checklist items as complete only when the production static output satisfies the rule.
